summary: # Cake Skirt Production Tutorial In this tutorial, we will learn how to create a cake skirt using Marvelous Designer. We will cover various aspects of the process, including panel creation, sewing techniques, and adjustments to ensure stability and a polished final product. ## 1. Creating the Base Panel First, we will only use the belt for our cake skirt, so we can delete the panels of the bag skirt. ### Drawing the Rectangle After deleting the unnecessary panels, let's draw a rectangle. This rectangle should be wider than the belt. The height of this rectangle can be aligned with the 2D window. ### Creating a Symmetrical Panel Next, create a symmetrical panel. Use the sewing tool to sew them together. Once sewn, press **Shift + F** to open the arrangement point, and arrange this panel on the arrangement point on the side. ## 2. Adjusting the Panel ### Filling Gaps After arranging the panel, you may notice some gaps between the body and the skirt. To address this, go to the attribute editor and pull the shoulder strap of the arrangement a little further. ### Simulation Settings Press the control key to start the simulation. After the simulation, if you observe that the wrinkles are very deep, you will need to reduce the particle diameter and collision thickness. Following this adjustment, the wrinkles should become smoother. ## 3. Layering for Stability ### Preparing for Multiple Layers As we are going to create a cake skirt with many layers, it is crucial to manage the wrinkles in the middle layer to prevent instability. Utilize the tail shrink rate for this purpose. ### Adding the Shrink Rate If you are unsure how to add the shrink rate, use the edit texture tool after selecting a panel. The arrow direction will show a gold shape. Since we want to shrink horizontally, we will reduce the tail shape. When reducing the shrink rate of the tail shape, you will notice that this panel will eventually become very flat and tight. Once this is achieved, freeze the panel and copy and paste it directly in the 3D or 2D window. ## 4. Rearranging and Sewing Layers ### Activating and Rearranging Panels After copying and pasting a layer of the panel, activate this panel and rearrange it. During the rearrangement, ensure to change the perspective to check for overlaps in other areas. If one arrangement point does not work, adjust other arrangement points accordingly. ### Sewing the Panels Re-use the line shrink tool to sew the panels together. Be cautious, as the top right corner is currently folded. Therefore, we must change the shrink line type to "turn." ### Finalizing the Simulation After opening the simulation, you will find that it is particularly stable at this point. Now, you can adjust the length of the outer panel. ## 5. Simulating Inner Layers ### Activating Inner Panels Next, activate the inner panel and simulate it together with the outer layer. Gradually change the tail shrink rate of the inner layer, paying attention to use time as a unit. Simulate and enlarge gradually; avoid making too large adjustments at once to prevent instability. ## 6. Adjusting the Belt ### Addressing the Belt Issue After completing the three-layer structure, if you activate the belt and open the simulation, you will notice that the belt falls down due to the weight of the other fabrics. To prevent the belt from deforming, we need to copy a fabric and change the attribute of this fabric to **Fusible Rigid**. ### Importance of Fusible Rigid The **Fusible Rigid** setting will cause the fabric to gradually shrink inwards, and it won’t be as strong as it was before. ## 7. Final Adjustments ### Increasing Skirt Size You may be curious about how to adjust the skirt if you want to increase its size. It’s quite simple! For a rectangular skirt, you just need to stretch it slightly to add creases. However, be careful not to pull too much at once. If you pull excessively, the skirt may be pierced, resulting in an unstable final simulation. --- This concludes the tutorial on creating a cake skirt in Marvelous Designer. Follow these steps carefully to ensure a well-structured and stable garment. Happy designing!
